intro: West Bromwich Albion forward Aune Heggebo has been suspended for two matches by The Football Association after scoring a goal in which the ball was handled in a fixture involving Norwich City, BBC Sport reports. The disciplinary decision follows an incident that has drawn attention to the enforcement of handball rules in English football.

sections.heading: What the FA ruling says
sections.text:
According to BBC Sport, Aune Heggebo received a two-match suspension from the FA for netting a goal that involved handling the ball in the play against Norwich City. The ban reflects the governing body's disciplinary response to an event in which a goal was scored with the hand. While individual case paperwork and any written reasons from the FA are not reproduced here, the reported outcome is a short-term match suspension handed down by the association.

The FA is responsible for discipline across the English game and can impose bans for breaches of the Laws of the Game or misconduct. Retrospective action or disciplinary measures following on-field incidents are part of the association's remit, and short suspensions are a common sanction where a player's actions are judged to have violated the rules.
